name: Hydroxyzine
metabolism: Alcohol dehydrogenase forms cetirizine by oxidation; CYP3A4/5 also participates in metabolism. Cetirizine is an active antihistamine and is eliminated substantially through the kidneys.
summary: Hydroxyzine is a first-generation piperazine antihistamine used to treat itching, anxiety, insomnia, and nausea. It can be taken by mouth or given by intramuscular injection.
toxicities: Drowsiness and dry mouth are reported; tremor and convulsions have been reported, usually at doses considerably above those recommended.
Postmarketing reports include QT prolongation and torsades de pointes.
Overdose most commonly causes hypersedation and may also cause convulsions, stupor, nausea, or vomiting; QT prolongation and torsades de pointes may occur.
generalRisks: The DailyMed oral tablet label contraindicates hydroxyzine in patients with prolonged QT and reports QT prolongation/torsades, especially with cardiac disease, electrolyte abnormalities, or other arrhythmogenic drugs. Hydroxyzine potentiates CNS depressants and may increase alcohol effects; drowsiness can impair driving. Overdose can cause severe sedation, convulsions, stupor, and QT/TdP. Rare serious skin reactions including AGEP have been reported.
saferUse: Do not combine with alcohol or other CNS depressants; avoid driving or dangerous machinery while drowsy or impaired.
Avoid use with known prolonged QT; review other QT-prolonging medicines and cardiac risk factors with a clinician.
Overdose can affect heart rhythm: seek urgent medical care after excess ingestion. Stop and seek medical advice for a new severe rash, fever, or signs of hypersensitivity.
dosageRemark: The DailyMed tablet label provides prescription dosing for anxiety, pruritus, and perioperative sedation. Those therapeutic regimens are not recreational dose guidance; recreational thresholds and duration are not established here.
